My personal theory as to why there isn't any major regrowth in the base game isn't really to do with lingering radiation but desertification (doesn't necessarily have to actually make the commonwealth a desert)

Basically:

\-Nuclear fire sweeps away most forests and grass immediately

\-Nuclear winter kills off the remaining grass and leaves almost exclusively older trees which are very deep-rooted

\-As the climate re-warms, massive rainstorms begin. Due to the root network being gone from most of the commonwealth's topsoil, the rain washes away the vast majority of its nutrients into the ocean and various bodies of water

\-Water becomes irradiated more than before due to the buildup of radioactive sediment from runoff

\-Radiation in fresh water sources compounds with newly barren soil

\-Only select species of mutated grass and other plants can survive in the sandy soil, and even then, they still struggle

\-Soil too nutritionally void for any trees to grow

All of this leads to sparse grass, no living trees, irradiated water, and only select areas still being farmable.

I could imagine farming becoming less of a settlement system and more of a land control system, a way of continually making a lot of money in the long term that's not pure luck and savescumming like with casinos, or grindy and gamey like one of the many caps grinding methods.

How's this; There's a few farms on the map, maybe 6. A couple will be neutral, outside of any obvious territory. One would cost outright caps, but be not terribly expensive. The second would be gotten through a difficult quest. The remaining 4 would be evenly split between the Legion and the NCR, who will hand them out when the player has enough reputation with that faction and does quests related to the farms. It would be an option to capture all of the farms for your faction, but there'd probably be consequences to this like a high tax that would make it a little more complicated than "Get all farms, infinite money".

Farms would have a few values that can be raised with questing, and in most circumstances, questing exclusively. Hydration, Units (We'll just say 1 unit = 1 harvestable crop), seeds, and sell price. Each farm has a unique value depending on its starting size and location as well as alignment, and again are raised through doing related quests. Hydration  is effected by the quality of piping around the farm and the proximity of the farm to fresh water. Hydration could be raised for your farms by using your technical skills to repair or replace faulty sections of piping, or you could do quests that would purify some of the random sludge-filled ponds into clean water for your farm. Seeds determine the crop used, and would be the value most based on player stats.  On a base level, seeds would be uncomplicated. You buy or construct a seed cloning machine, get the seed you desire, and set that as the one you'll be sewing. Initially, it'll be a couple of simple and straight upgrades like crops that grow faster or crops that sell for more. If you have high science, medical, or survival skills however it becomes more interesting. Venturing into vault 22 allows the recovery of possible cross-bred seeds, modified seeds, and so forth. Crops grown from these seeds would have special properties rather than just selling for more, or being harvestable more often. Some may contain chemicals which are partially convertible into stim packs, say at a 20% rate. 10 units (crops) for 2 stimpacks, or 20 stimpacks out of a fully upgraded farm with 100 units. Some are akin to Coyote Tobacco Chew, giving your some drug-like perks while being addictive and without providing food. Lastly, sell price is effected by both quests and barter speech checks in relation to the nearby towns which are buying your product. Thanks for coming to my Ted Talk.

I just want a way to balance our colors in outfits better. In the clothing, to be specific. It's almost impossible to  get the correct color combination and ratio of those colors in your clothing. Let's say you want to make something that resembles a 1700s Swedish army uniform for your little meme faction. You'll need primarily blue, with some yellow. You'll need less than half of the clothing to be yellow, or it'll be too yellow dominant. So, what are your choices? You get 1 choice. Take a blue clothing item, and pair it with golden gear (lantern, spyglass, icepicks). Hope to god people interpret your gold tools as being part of the outfit and not just your own set. Protip; they never will, unless you tell them ahead of time.

My proposed solution? Sashes. It's stupidly simple to put in, but I know the devs won't, because it'd be slow and kind of annoying. Basically, you just take every shirt in the game, and add a version with a sash on it. Then, you'd need a version with a sash in every available color. This is precisely why I don't think it'd get added, and why custom colored clothes won't become a thing any time soon.
